## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Harituccārachaḍḍana-sikkhāpada* is the ninth rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun commits an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) if she throws or causes to be thrown feces, urine, rubbish, or food scraps onto green cultivated plants (*harite*) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. It immediately follows the eighth rule (*Pācittiya* 8), sharing an identical structure except for replacing waste disposal "over a wall or fence" (*tirokuḍḍe vā tiropākāre vā*) with disposal "on cultivated greens/crops" (*harite*) [Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997]. 

Although there is no equivalent *pācittiya* rule for fully ordained monks, the commentary *Samantapāsādikā* notes that committing this act constitutes a *dukkaṭa* (wrongdoing) for monks [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offense clauses (*anāpatti*) outlined in the rule provide exemptions if a nun deposits the waste at the edge of the field, if she has requested and obtained permission from the field's owner, or if she has inspected the area beforehand [Hüsken 1997]. Buddhaghosa's *Samantapāsādikā* discusses the regulation in detail, clarifying the definition of planted, cultivated land (*ropima*) such as coconut groves or agricultural fields [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide transmission across Vinaya lineages, including parallel rules in the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahāsaṅghika traditions (extant in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit recensions, such as Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda *Pācittiya* 139 and 140), alongside the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral; Bechert et al. 1997]. DharmaNexus records significant internal formulaic reuse across 87 Pali texts, sharing the closest recurring Vinaya phraseology with *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 54, *Pācittiya* 8, and *Pācittiya* 62, along with cross-language alignments to Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* texts [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
